summary: The claim and proof are correct. Base-negation symmetry makes every actual fiber a subset of the positive-volume zero fiber and places the original marginal mean in that fiber. The volume hypothesis gives domination of the original marginal by M times the uniform law on the zero fiber. The accepted scalar projection bound applies with the explicit centroid, covariance, translation, and standard-deviation normalization stated in the proof. The density-height and variance estimates yield both original own-mean cap bounds, and the paired-base argument transfers them to every containing closed mixed halfspace at the same fixed point. Positive volume, zero-volume fibers, d=1, zero continuous normals, and closed boundaries are all covered.
